script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for March 1. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Enter a rainforest and life surrounds you—above, below, on every surface.  More species live in one rainforest tree than in entire temperate forests.  These jungles cover just 6% of Earth yet host more than half of all known species.

A single hectare—about 2.5 acres—of Amazon rainforest can contain 400 tree species. All of North America has roughly 700. Rainforests are biodiversity factories, producing new species through millennia of stable conditions and fierce competition. Rainforests have distinct layers—forest floor, understory, canopy, and emergent layer—each with its own climate and residents.  Some animals spend their entire lives in a single layer, never touching the ground or seeing the sky.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: The right conditions create abundance.  Warmth, water, stability—when these align, life explodes.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Conditions Audit - Design for Flourishing.

Here's your activity: What are your rainforest conditions—the environments, situations, or relationships where you thrive most? List them. Then ask: how can I spend more time in these conditions? How can I bring these conditions into other areas of my life? This helps you identify and create conditions that help you thrive.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why jungles are so alive can be applied to conditions audit - design for flourishing. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
